comment: Spec 055 §9.2. The calibration reference, the gate budgets and the memory-bound parameters of the ts-wire-passivity job. reference_ns is the minimum of 30 runs of lib/common.mjs workload(), the median of three fresh processes, on the reference machine. A change to it, to the workload, to a budget or to a memory parameter is a reviewed diff, never a silent recalibration.

calibration.workload: 20,000 Map.set and property updates and integer-to-string conversions (lib/common.mjs workload)

memory.comment: Small configured bounds so that saturation is reached. Each arm runs `batches` equal batches; the first `warmup_batches` are warm-up. Per batch, the excess is the arm's RSS over the baseline arm's at the same batch. Bound on the excess: the shared buffers' maximum length plus entry_bytes per exchange slot (the hook's WeakMap entry and state object), the Fabric worker's isolate and slack for allocator noise. Linear growth: the last batch's excess may exceed the highest excess of the first half after warm-up by at most growth_bytes (a one-time allocator step that stays flat is not growth); the main thread's heap after GC may grow by at most heap_growth_bytes.

recorder.comment: Unit 055-t13. The whole recorder (install(), the capture pipeline and the sender) under a paced fan-out of `clients` clients. stalled_recorder: each arm (a stalled disk fsync, a Node that never answers, a redaction service that never answers, the spool's admission lock held, a saturated capture worker; unit 055-t16: a full disk whose losses only the loss ledger holds, and that with the ledger's header lock held by another process) runs `rounds` rounds of `duration_ms` against the baseline arm; the application's requests may fall at most to throughput_min_ratio of the baseline's, every response's bytes and every cancelled stream's error must equal the baseline's, nothing may reach the application (error, rejection, stderr byte), and the event-loop budgets above apply to the median deltas. sustained: the recorder for sustained_ms with one 40 MiB mutable request, against the same workload with no capture, judged by the event-loop budgets.
